text:
Scott Morrow spent a long stretch as a healthy scratch before the Rangers put him back in, and he has given them reason to keep him there. The Hockey News wrote about him "seizing his opportunity," and The New York Times asked whether he had earned a spot once the team is healthy.

The sample is six games, so treat everything loosely, but the shape is good. With him on the ice at five on five, New York has taken 55.1% of shot attempts and 61.6% of expected goals, nearly ten points better than without him. He has one assist and 12 shots in about 13 minutes a night.

The puck-moving profile is what makes him interesting. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 46% of his entries last season, and a third of his shots came off the rush (typical for defensemen is 17%). The worry is the other end: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on in 2025-26, in a small sample. Watch whether the defensive side holds up as his minutes stabilize.
headline: Morrow has made the most of his chance
